turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anika? Come in, grab a seat. I'm tight on time, so what's the main problem today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, hi. So, um, I'm pregnant, and I've started spotting, and there's these cramps, and I barely slept. My partner Josh is stuck out in the waiting room.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many weeks?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the thing, I don't actually know. Could be eight weeks, could be ten. The last period was around Diwali, or after. We had everyone over, my sister came up from Geelong, and I never wrote the date down.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Positive test when?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Home test about two weeks ago, a faint line, then a proper one the next morning. The GP did a blood test after that. I was going to tell Mum on the weekend, and then this started.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): The spotting. How heavy?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Not heavy. Brown, just on a liner. It's been a week... no, three days. I keep counting from Saturday and that's wrong.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any clots?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No clots. A bit of pink this morning, then brown again. Sorry, I talk too much when I'm nervous.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Cramps, low down, both sides, like a period. Mild. I still went to work yesterday, I do the desk at the library, and the returns machine jammed, which did nothing for my mood.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Score it, zero to ten.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Three. Maybe four if I stand up quick. Not doubling-over pain.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain just on one side?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Both sides, low.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shoulder-tip pain?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I slept funny on the couch the other night.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes, not really. More just queasy, and coffee makes it worse.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizzy or faint?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit light-headed getting out of bed this morning. I didn't faint. Sat on the edge of the bed and it passed.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Diarrhoea?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Bowels are normal. I had a weird dream about the library, but that's not medical.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't feel hot, I checked.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): First pregnancy?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. We weren't not trying, exactly. I'm twenty-nine, and Mum thinks that's young, but Josh calls it seeing what happens.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any operations?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never had surgery. Wisdom teeth don't count, do they? They were out in the chair, not a hospital.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Other medical problems?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really. A few weeks back the GP did a thyroid blood test and they said it was borderline. No number, just borderline, and they'd repeat it later. I felt fine.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medicines. Folic acid?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I thought I had the five milligram ones, but no, I checked the bottle this morning, it's five hundred micrograms, once a day. The purple Blackmores.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else? Nurofen, Panadol?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I took Nurofen for the cramps. Two tablets... no, one tablet, the two hundred milligram one, yesterday, and then I remembered I shouldn't, so I stopped. No Panadol.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines or anything else?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of. Josh is the one with the hayfever.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. Can't stand it. Josh vapes on the balcony, which I hate, but that's him, not me.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped when the test was positive. Last drink was a glass of wine at my cousin's wedding, before I knew. Nothing since.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. I'll do observations and have a feel of your tummy. Want him in?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes please. He's probably pacing. The coffee machine out there is broken, so at least he can't buy that sludge.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Josh? Come through. From what you've seen, how heavy is the bleeding and how long for?
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, parking's a joke on this street. The bleeding's been going a week, quite heavy, like a period. Cramps were that bad she could barely walk from the car.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Josh, that's not right. It's spotting, not a period, three days, and I walked in fine. The cramps are mild. You're making it sound worse.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): So I'm hearing somewhere between three days and a week, and you two don't agree on the amount. Did she faint?
[SEG0051] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She nearly did, this morning. I heard her sit down hard. She's been white as a sheet.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): I didn't nearly faint. I was light-headed and I sat down on purpose. You weren't even in the room.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Light-headed, not a collapse. Any bleeding in the last hour?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): The liner's barely marked. I changed it before we left.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Lie back. Tummy's soft. Mild tenderness low down, both sides. No guarding.
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure 112 over 68. Pulse 92. Temperature 36.7.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 92 high? I get nervy in clinics. I also had a small latte, which I know is not my best habit.
[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's a bit up, fine for now. This is most likely a threatened miscarriage, but I can't rule out an ectopic until we scan. Working impression, not a diagnosis.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Ectopic is the tube one, right? My friend Priya had a miscarriage last year and she reckoned the waiting was the worst bit, and her mum kept bringing soup.
[SEG0060] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, outside the uterus. We need to see where the pregnancy is and if there's a heartbeat.
[SEG0061] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Can she work? She was meant to go in this arvo.
[SEG0062] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today. Rest, no heavy lifting. Continue the folic acid, five hundred micrograms daily. No more Nurofen, no anti-inflammatories.
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Scan today in the early pregnancy unit, a pelvic ultrasound. Bloods today as well: pregnancy hormone, blood group and antibodies, and a full blood count.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): Will the scan hurt? I haven't drunk enough water, they always want a full bladder, and I've been to the loo twice from nerves.
[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): They'll sort the bladder. It isn't painful. They'll fit you in today.
[SEG0066] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if it's bad news?
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then we talk straight after. I'll see you back this afternoon with the scan and the blood results.
[SEG0068] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the bleeding soaks a pad within an hour, the pain becomes severe, or you feel faint, come straight back to emergency, don't wait for the afternoon.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Pad an hour, severe pain, or faint, emergency. I'll try not to google. Thanks for squeezing us in, I know you're flat out.

spec.situation: Woman about 8-10 weeks pregnant with spotting and cramps; unsure of dates ('the last period was around Diwali, or after'); anxious; partner waits outside then joins. Scan and blood tests planned today, strict return advice.
features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
